pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with a CHECK on the three values. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks that the seeded rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected. Seeding happens in 0001, so this exercises the ALTER on existing rows.
src/index.js `item` renders ' — high' or ' — low' and nothing for normal. Test 'AC-2' asserts the exact list.
The query uses WHERE priority = ? ORDER BY id. Test 'AC-3' covers high (ids 3 and 1 set, listed in id order), low and normal.
The unfiltered query is ORDER BY id. Test 'AC-4' asserts the full list.
The `nav` function renders All, High, Normal and Low, with the current one in <strong>. Test 'AC-5' asserts the exact nav for all four views.
A present but invalid priority, including an empty one, returns 400 before any query. Test 'AC-6' covers High, urgent, empty and __proto__, and asserts there is no <li>.

The code uses a COUNT query to choose between 'No

-priority items.' and 'No items yet.'. Test 'AC-7' covers high, low and normal with no match, and the empty table in all four views.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. Test 'AC-8' asserts it. The traffic worker appends the path, query included, to the request URL. The config check now accepts a query.

findings.what: The README describes the filter but not the filter links or the '— high'/'— low' labels in the list.
findings.fix: Add one sentence on the labels and the All/High/Normal/Low links.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent. Nothing was added beyond the spec, apart from the traffic-config check change that AC-8 needs, which the PR discloses.
All 8 acceptance items are met and every States row has a test. The spec has a dated go and decisions, and no commit edits an acceptance item.

npm test could not run here because vitest is not installed. By reading, the tests assert behaviour and would fail on broken code. The test setup resets the database before each test, and the traffic fake app and the traffic-config shell test were extended consistently.
README and CLAUDE.md are broadly consistent. The only gap is the low-severity README finding.
The query is parameterised and the 400 check runs before any query. The migration is additive and backward-compatible with the previous app, which selects only title.
The priority value is checked against an allow-list and bound as a parameter. Titles are still escaped. The loosened route regex still refuses spaces and '#'.
The diff changes a server-rendered page whose only markup is a plain nav and list, with no UI component or style files.
No browser or preview exists in this session; the diff touches no UI framework files.
The title is within 72 characters. The claims match the diff: tests not loosened, the traffic-config check change disclosed, the migration described, the README updated.
